title: Microsoft Purview DLP: delegate Copilot and Cowork policies to administrative units
summary: The briefing incorrectly says cross-unit investigations require an unrestricted administrator: restricted administrators can cover multiple assigned units. Narrow that requirement to organisation-wide views; the policy scoping, prerequisites and PowerShell call are otherwise supported.

claims.claim: Purview DLP is extending administrative unit support to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention is extending Administrative Units support to Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The change delegates supported Copilot DLP policy management to assigned-unit administrators without tenant-wide permissions.
claims.quote: delegate management of supported Copilot DLP policies to administrators within their assigned Administrative Units, supporting regional, departmental, and regulatory boundaries without granting tenant-wide policy-management permissions.

An administrative unit is a subset of the Entra directory, typically organised by business group or geographic area.
claims.quote: Administrative units are subsets of your Microsoft Entra ID directory and are created for the purposes of managing collections of users, groups, distribution groups, and accounts. These collections are typically created along business group lines or geopolitical areas.

claims.claim: Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork DLP policies can be scoped to administrative units.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location supports administrative units for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; What's changing
claims.claim: Policy unit selection is at Microsoft Purview portal > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units.
claims.quote:
go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
2. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy, and enter a name and description.
3. On the Admin units page, select the administrative units for the policy.

claims.claim: The Copilot policy location is available only in the Custom policy template.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location is only available in the Custom policy template.

claims.claim: After unit selection, administrators select the Copilot location and include or exclude users and groups within those units.
claims.quote: Select the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location and choose the users and groups to include or exclude within the selected administrative units.

claims.claim: Restricted administrators can select only assigned units and manage policies within that scope.
claims.quote: An administrative unit restricted administrator can select only their assigned units and manage policies within that scope.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Unrestricted administrators can select units or keep Full directory, the default entire-directory scope.
claims.quote: Unrestricted administrators don't have to select administrative units as part of the policy configuration. They can keep the default of the entire directory or select one or more administrative units.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The new administrative-unit control is admin-opt-in rather than automatically replacing existing policy scope.
claims.quote: Existing tenant-wide policies continue to apply, and configuration is optional for organizations choosing to use Administrative Unit (AU)-scoped management.

claims.claim: Copilot and Cowork DLP scoping follows the prompt submitter rather than the file or email owner.
claims.quote: DLP policy scoping for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork is based on the user who submits the prompt, not the owner of a file or email that the experience accesses.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn's Finance example applies the Finance policy even when Finance users access content owned outside Finance.
claims.quote: a policy scoped to the Finance administrative unit applies to Finance users' Copilot and Cowork interactions, even when they access content owned by someone outside Finance.

claims.claim: Users outside the units selected for a policy are not eligible for that policy.
claims.quote: When restricted administrators create or edit policies that support administrative units, they can select administrative units so that only the users in those administrative units are eligible for the policy

claims.claim: Assigning units to role-group members requires the Role management role.
claims.quote: To assign a role group member to an administrative unit, administrators must be assigned the Role management role.

claims.claim: Unit assignment is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users > Assign admin units.
claims.quote:
On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.
... If the selected users or groups need to be assigned to administrative units, select the users or groups and select Assign admin units.
claims.fix: Expand controls[1].ui.path and its rendered table path to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users > Assign admin units', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions. The omitted wizard-page heading does not change the destination.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for assigning administrative units to Purview role-group members.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview role group member assign administrative units PowerShell API Set-RoleGroup PolicyRBACScopes; "Purview" "Assign admin units" "PowerShell" role group member. Opened Purview permissions, Purview admin units and Add-RoleGroupMember reference; no assignment operation documented.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy-name> -PolicyRBACScopes <administrative-unit-GUIDs> assigns units to a new DLP policy.
claims.quote:
The Name parameter specifies the unique name of the DLP policy.
... The PolicyRBACScopes parameter specifies the administrative units to assign to the policy.

claims.claim: PolicyRBACScopes accepts Entra administrative unit ObjectID GUIDs, with multiple values separated by commas.
claims.quote: A valid value is the Microsoft Entra ObjectID (GUID value) of the administrative unit. You can specify multiple values separated by commas.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy is documented in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
